findings.reason: The protected source is the complete canonical solution: a positive pile is winning exactly when it is not divisible by four. The one-line predicate directly expresses the proved invariant, is maximally clear and concise, and admits no material candidate improvement.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 292 and its Python positive-integer-to-boolean contract. The Reference preserves the turn order, legal removals, last-stone win condition, optimal-play question, all three examples in order and the sole explanation, and the complete 32-bit positive constraint.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064318000. Its method and the app-local solve function return the identical modulo-four predicate; only the LeetCode class wrapper differs.

The legal 2,000/8,000/32,000-stone tiers span 16x and remain far below the 32-bit maximum while preserving a losing multiple-of-four result. The current source passes at -0.01 relative exponent and 1.03x largest ratio; a correct linear implementation that tabulates the invariant through every pile size passes all outputs but fails only scaling at +0.92 and 245.79x.

The Approach proves both directions of the multiple-of-four invariant with complementary moves, states constant time and space, and now presents the linear dynamic program, recursive game tree, smallest winning piles, and positive-domain boundary as explicit alternatives and edge cases.

The hash-bound public Reference remains verified against its reviewed source evidence, preserving all three examples and their explanation presence, the sole constraint, the exact game rules, and the zero-visual structure.
